Hi Asha — thanks for the heads up.

High level plan (summary):

1) Sampling methodology
- We will perform a stratified random sample across tenant size (small/medium/large) and geozone (US/EU/APAC). For this run we propose 12 tenants (4 per zone, spread across size bins).
- For each tenant we pull: active KV snapshots (prefixes), deletion event logs covering the retention window, hashlist snapshots for object stores, and a KMS attestation for the keys used during the period.

2) Artifact list (what you should expect)
- hashlist-<tenant>-YYYYMMDD.txt (SHA256 hashes for stored objects)
- deletion-log-<tenant>-YYYYMMDD.log (timestamped deletion events with request id)
- kv-snapshot-<tenant>-YYYYMMDD.tar.gz (metadata/keys for prefixes)
- kms-attestation-<tenant>.pdf (signed statement from our KMS team)
- chain-of-custody.txt (who packaged/transferred what)

3) Delivery & timeline
- We will produce a sanitized sample bundle by Tuesday, May 25 EOD (sanitization removes PII and replaces tenant IDs with canonical tokens).
- Final full auditor bundle (if auditor needs more than the sample) can be delivered via secure SFTP or encrypted courier by Jun 4–6 depending on size.

I attached a tiny "sample_manifest.csv" and a proposed "sampling_matrix.xlsx" to illustrate the bins. Marcus — can you confirm the retention-window mapping and whether the KMS attestation can be generated on our side by May 25?

Regards,
Sofia
Sofia Ivanova

Sofia / Asha — quick clarifications and confirmables: 

- Retention mapping: we will use the tenant's committed TTL and any contractual overrides. For FinSecure the relevant retention window is 13 months (contractual + legal hold checks). We'll include a small mapping table in the bundle.
- KMS attestation: yes — KMS can provide a signed attestation (key IDs, creation dates, and statement of non-reuse for deleted keys) by May 25.
- Artifact sources: deletion logs are pulled from the tenant lifecycle service (path: s3://redwood-lifecycle-audit/YYYY/MM/DD), hashlists are generated by the background job hash-exporter-2; snapshots come from the KV-exporter job.

I also added note re: chain-of-custody: we recommend at-rest encryption + a signed manifest and MD5/SHA256 checksums for the archive. If the auditor requires physical media, we can use our vendor courier (insured, tracked).

I'll drop the small mapping file and a short README into the Drive folder by EOD Sun.

— Marcus
